rendered_html: 📔 Regulatory Bulletin — 16 October 2026 (Weekly) Executive Summary • Singapore payment-services enforcement benchmark: MAS revoked Sir Money Changer’s licence after finding that a third party operated cross-border transfers under its name and that false or misleading information was provided. The case is an analogous third-party and licence-perimeter control benchmark, not a Hong Kong requirement. • UK remediation benchmark: The FCA’s motor-finance compensation scheme remains partly suspended pending a February 2027 legal challenge. Lenders must continue the specified preparation and complaints activity; this is a UK comparison, not a Hong Kong obligation. They do not establish Hong Kong requirements. 🟡 MAS revokes Sir Money Changer’s Major Payment Institution Licence 🇸🇬 Item ID: item-20261014-mas-regulatory-announcements-c9fb3222f6 ⏰ Deadline: Licence revocation effective 15 September 2026; no additional source deadline stated Products: Payments, FX, Cross-border transfers MAS revoked Sir Money Changer Pte. Ltd.’s Major Payment Institution Licence under the Payment Services Act 2019, effective 15 September 2026. MAS says the firm can no longer provide cross-border money-transfer or money-changing services and that its investigation found a third party independently operated a cross-border transfer business under the firm’s name at one of its places of business. MAS also found that the firm provided false or misleading information, and states that licensees must not let third parties use their licences and payment providers must maintain effective oversight and control. The final Singapore case is an analogous benchmark for third-party oversight and licence-perimeter governance, not a Hong Kong obligation. Source: MAS Revokes the Major Payment Institution License of Sir Money Changer Pte Ltd 🟡 FCA motor-finance legal challenge set for February 2027 🇬🇧 Item ID: item-20261013-fca-benchmark-a35220ff44 ⏰ Deadline: UK Upper Tribunal hearing: 16–26 February 2027; judgment expected in the following months Products: Lending, Complaints handling, Customer remediation The FCA says legal challenges to its motor-finance compensation scheme will be heard by the Upper Tribunal from 16 to 26 February 2027, with judgment expected in the following months. The scheme is partly suspended, but the FCA says lenders must continue preparing for provisions that remain in force and progress complaints as far as possible, including specified consumer letters. The FCA expects lenders to plan rigorously for a possible quashing, make necessary financial provisions and engage auditors; normal complaints statutory timescales could resume in that scenario. This remains an active UK legal process and a customer-remediation and operational-readiness benchmark only, not a Hong Kong requirement. Source: Motor finance legal challenge to be heard in February 2027 Primary source: official document Watch List • Monitor the Upper Tribunal judgment and any FCA statement on the motor-finance compensation scheme after the February 2027 hearing. • Monitor whether MAS publishes further action concerning Sir Money Changer or the third-party operation identified in its enforcement notice. Weekly Trend This restricted rework retains two overseas control benchmarks: MAS’s final licence action highlights third-party licence-perimeter oversight, while the FCA’s live litigation highlights remediation, complaint-handling and provisioning contingency planning. Neither establishes a Hong Kong requirement.
